title: Arrange the mantra
prompt: Put the words of Ganesha's seed mantra in order.
why: Om Gam Ganapataye Namah — Om, the seed syllable Gam, 'to Ganapati', 'salutations'. Gam (गं) is Ganesha's bija.

title: Arrange the shloka
prompt: Order the first line of the Vakratunda shloka.
why: 'Curved-trunked, great-bodied, radiant as ten million suns' — the invocation recited before beginning any work.

title: Arrange the shloka
prompt: Order the second line of the Vakratunda shloka.
why: 'Make my endeavours free of obstacles, O Lord, in all works, always.'

title: The birth of Ganesha
prompt: Put the events of Ganesha's birth story in order.
items: Parvati shapes a boy from turmeric paste
The boy guards the door while she bathes
Shiva is stopped and severs the boy's head
Ganas bring the head of an elephant
Shiva names him Ganapati, lord of the ganas
why: The story teaches loyalty to one's word, the mother's love, and how Ganesha became the first to be worshipped.

title: The race around the world
prompt: Order the events of the race between Ganesha and Kartikeya.
items: Narada brings a single fruit of wisdom
Whoever circles the world thrice first wins
Kartikeya flies off on his peacock
why: 'My parents are my whole world' — insight wins over speed.

title: Ashtavinayak yatra
prompt: Arrange the first four Ashtavinayak temples in traditional pilgrimage order.
why: The yatra begins at Morgaon (Mayureshwar), then Siddhatek, Pali (Ballaleshwar), Mahad (Varadvinayak), Theur, Lenyadri, Ozar and Ranjangaon, returning to Morgaon.

title: Ashtavinayak yatra
prompt: Arrange the last four Ashtavinayak temples in pilgrimage order.
why: Theur (Chintamani), Lenyadri (Girijatmaj), Ozar (Vighnahar) and Ranjangaon (Mahaganapati) complete the eight.

title: The eight avatars
prompt: Order the first four avatars of the Mudgala Purana.
why: Vakratunda (defeats Matsara/envy), Ekadanta (Madasura/pride), Mahodara (Mohasura/delusion), Gajanana (Lobhasura/greed).

title: The eight avatars
prompt: Order the last four avatars of the Mudgala Purana.
why: Lambodara (Krodhasura/anger), Vikata (Kamasura/lust), Vighnaraja (Mamasura/ego), Dhumravarna (Abhimanasura/attachment).

title: Ganesh Chaturthi
prompt: Put the festival's rituals in the order they happen.
items: The clay idol is brought home
why: The deity is welcomed as a guest, given life, honoured daily, and finally bid farewell — 'come again early next year'.

title: The moon's laughter
prompt: Order the events of the Chandra story.
items: Mooshika stumbles at a snake and Ganesha falls
His belly bursts; he ties it with the snake
why: From this comes the custom of not looking at the moon on Chaturthi night.

title: Writing the Mahabharata
prompt: Order the events of the epic's dictation.
items: Vyasa seeks a scribe who can keep pace
Ganesha agrees if Vyasa never pauses
Vyasa asks that Ganesha understand each verse first
He snaps off his tusk and writes on
why: Ekadanta — the one-tusked — earned through devotion to knowledge.

title: Ganesha Gayatri
prompt: Arrange the Ganesha Gayatri mantra.
why: 'We know the one-tusked, we meditate on the curved-trunked; may the tusked one inspire us.'

title: Gajananam shloka
prompt: Order the lines of the Gajananam verse.
why: Elephant-faced, served by the hosts; eater of wood-apple and jambu; Uma's son, destroyer of sorrow; I bow to Vighneshwara's lotus feet.

title: Kubera's feast
prompt: Order the events of Kubera's feast.
items: Proud Kubera invites Ganesha to a feast
Ganesha eats everything in the kitchen and store
He starts eating the palace itself
A humble handful of rice from Shiva satisfies him
why: Love outweighs wealth: what all of Kubera's riches could not do, a devoted handful did.

title: Making modaks
prompt: Order the steps of ukadiche modak.
items: Cook jaggery and coconut for the filling
Knead rice-flour dough with hot water
Shape cups, fill, and pinch the pleats
why: Twenty-one steamed modaks are the classic Chaturthi offering.

title: Twelve names
prompt: Arrange these names in the order of the Sankashtanashana Stotra.
why: The stotra opens: Sumukhash-chaikadantash-cha Kapilo Gajakarnakah, followed by Lambodara, Vikata, Vighnanasha, Vinayaka, Dhumraketu, Ganadhyaksha, Bhalachandra, Gajanana.

title: Sukhakarta Dukhaharta
prompt: Order the opening lines of the aarti.
why: Bringer of joy, remover of sorrow and obstacles; showering love and grace; beautiful, anointed with sindoor; a pearl garland gleaming at the neck.

title: Puja steps
prompt: Order these steps of the shodashopachara puja.
why: Sixteen offerings treat the deity as an honoured guest: invited, bathed, dressed, fed, and celebrated with light.

title: Ganesha's family
prompt: Order these from Ganesha's grandparents to his sons.
why: Parvati is Himavan's daughter; Ganesha's sons in the northern tradition are Shubha (auspiciousness) and Labha (gain).
